sources.entry: Request Tracker - Enterprise-grade issue tracking system. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 Perl

summary.one_liner: Request Tracker (RT) is an open source, enterprise-grade issue and ticket tracking system written in Perl that helps organizations track tasks, owners, and completion history.
summary.what_it_does: RT lets organizations track what needs to get done, who is working on which tasks, what has already been done, and when tasks were or were not completed. It is organized around queues, and it receives email through a mail gateway that pipes incoming messages into RT. The README describes a web interface, a web installer (rt-server), and command-line utilities for session cleanup, digest emails, dashboard emails, and scheduled processes. Ticket relationship graphing uses graphviz, and dashboard emails with charts need a Chrome-based browser. Full-text search is supported when the database has full-text indexing configured. Users, groups, queues, scrips, and access control are set up after installation.
use_cases: Track IT helpdesk or support requests
Assign and follow tasks across a team
Run scheduled ticket automation such as auto-resolving old tickets
Self-host an issue tracker with Perl and a SQL database
how_to_run: Unpack the distribution: tar xzvf rt.tar.gz
Run ./configure (see ./configure --help for options; default install is /opt/rt6)
Run make testdeps, then make fixdeps to install missing Perl modules
Run make install, then make initialize-database (or use the web installer via /opt/rt6/sbin/rt-server)
Configure a web server with FastCGI or mod_perl, and set up cron jobs and the mail gateway as described in the README
Change the default root/password credentials before use
stack: MySQL 8.0.31+ / MariaDB 10.6+ / PostgreSQL 13+ / Oracle 18c+ / SQLite (testing only)
Apache with mod_fcgid or mod_perl, nginx, or another FastCGI-capable server
Chrome-based browser (optional, for dashboard chart emails)
notable: Enterprise-grade ticket tracking under GPL v2 with no licensing cost at any scale
Supports several production databases, including MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, and Oracle
Email gateway (rt-mailgate) lets queues be reached by sending mail to addresses
Scheduled processes and digest/dashboard emails run via cron-style jobs
Includes a make-based dependency checker (make testdeps / make fixdeps) and documented upgrade paths
caveats: Commercial support, hosting, and training are offered by Best Practical; the README recommends a support contract for heavy or mission-critical use
Full-text search is slow unless database full-text indexing is set up, and it is disabled by default
SQLite is for testing only with no upgrade path guaranteed; the default /opt/rt6 install path does not work under SELinux's default configuration
